text: These professional soldiers are the regular troops of the kingdom, funded by the royal household. Enjoying a fixed wage and standardized equipment, and trained uniformly, they far outmatch conscripted peasants, and even most knights' squires, in large-scale combat.

The Knights of the Round Table are the most illustrious among Grail Champions—great knights whose names shall be inscribed in history, living saints whose deeds seem miraculous to mortal eyes, and legends sung across generations in the ballads of Bretonnia.

In a Bretonnia rife with bandits and brigands, not every knight follows the traditional path. These Errantry Knights hold wealth as the greatest virtue, arming themselves with the finest equipment money can buy, serving as a formidable force for whoever pays the highest price.

The Knights of the Order of the Northern Marches are Bretonnia's vanguard against the forces of Chaos from the north. Often dispatched as crusaders to the frontlines of the Empire or Kislev to aid their human allies against the wicked forces of Chaos, they seek neither gold nor glory—only to uphold the true virtues of chivalry.

The Knights of the Order of the Lion are among Bretonnia's most venerable knightly orders, regarded by the nobility as the very embodiment of honor and nobility. The Order holds the wealthy castles of the western coast, nurturing the most promising youths destined to become Grail Knights.

The Knights of the Order of the Boar are stationed for generations in southern Bretonnia. Raised amid the forests, these warriors have waged prolonged wars against the fiercest beasts, the fickle Wood Elves, and the vile Greenskins, making them Bretonnia's most ruthless hunters.

The Knights of the Order of the Pegasus are the glorious warband of Parravon. The Pegasus Knights typically charge into battle astride their sacred steeds, but when the Lady and the realm have need, these noble knights shall just as readily set foot upon the ground.

The Bastion Sergeants are the private soldiers of Bretonnia's feudal lords. These men are usually of humble birth, unable to attain the status of knighthood, but through outstanding performance, they may be selected by their lord to serve within the castle, receiving professional training and equipment to rival that of knights. Even a great city like Parravon fields only 500 Bastion Sergeants—few in number, yet still the backbone of Bretonnian lords' infantry lines.
The Guardians of the Holy Tomb are core members of the knightly orders, entrusted with guarding the resting places of Bretonnia's legendary figures immortalized in history.
